item.title: Ian Rush calls out bizarre Alexander Isak criticism after electric start rivals Haaland
item.description: Ian Rush calls out bizarre Alexander Isak criticism after electric start rivals Haaland Ian Rush has disagreed with the common consensus about Alexander Isak this season. The Swedish international has been accused, at various times this season, of not being actively involved during Liverpool games. But Alexander Isak is scoring – and that’s what matters! (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) As Rush was at pains to point out, the former Newcastle United hitman is scoring goals this season. Enough, at any rate, to put him in early contention with Manchester City’s Erling Haaland for the golden boot, with seven Premier League goals registered to the Norwegian’s nine – and in one fewer game to boot. “People say that Isak isn’t getting involved much but he’s scoring goals and that’s all that matters. The hardest thing in football is to score a goal and he’s only second to (Erling) Haaland,” the Liverpool legend told BBC Sport . It seems that no matter what the 27-year-old does in the famous red shirt, someone will have something negative to say about his performances. But the fact remains that Isak is managing to get on the scoresheet with some degree of frequency as part of a frontline that is far from cohesive at this stage. Can you imagine how many times he’ll be finding the back of the net once he finds a collective rhythm alongside Cody Gakpo and Bradley Barcola? Critics forget what Isak went through at Liverpool last term (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) One may reasonably be inclined to think that critics have forgotten how Isak had the debut season from hell at Liverpool following his move from Newcastle in the summer. The forward managed only 1,032 minutes across all competitions in Arne Slot’s final season in charge, between adductor issues and a broken fibula. 1,032 minutes, four goals and one assist. In 2026/27, the Swede has already racked up eight goals and an assist in 899 minutes of action (across all competitions). Far easier for Alexander Isak to build fluency when he’s spending a lot more time on the pitch early in the season and stringing a series of starts together from one game to the next.

item.title: Official: Brock Faber Returns to MN Wild Blue Line
item.description: Nick Wosika-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Wild are in Boston on Saturday trying to add more points to their already gawdy total of 32, the most in both the Central Division and Western Conference. Entering tonight’s matchup, the Wild have a 98% chance of making the playoffs , according to multiple models and sportsbooks. Even more impressive, they’ve done it all without top-line defenseman, Brock Faber. The former Gopher fractured his skull on Sept. 25 when a puck hit him in the side of the head during the Wild’s preseason finale against Dallas. He had surgery two days later, spent three days at Regions Hospital and has missed all 21 regular season games since. Doctors cleared Faber to practice in early November. By Nov. 12, head coach John Hynes confirmed that the target date for his return was Saturday, but there were “no guarantees.” As recent as Friday, there were real doubts over whether or not Faber would hit that date, or wait Tuesday when the Wild return home against Nashville. Minnesota Wild activate Brock Faber for his season debut But then Saturday morning, the Wild made it official, activating Faber from injured reserve, and announcing on social media that the 24-year-old defenseman is back. Hynes confirmed the debut, according to Joe O’Donnell (Wild radio). Michael Russo (The Athletic) reported that Joel Eriksson Ek will play as well. The #mnwild has activated defenseman Brock Faber from Injured Reserve. — Minnesota Wild PR (@mnwildPR) November 14, 2026 we can think of exactly 7 reasons to be happy today — Minnesota Wild (@minnesotawild) November 14, 2026 Related: MN Wild Getting Healthier Again; Faber Back…? The defense pairs aren’t set yet. Russo listed two options , with Faber skating next to either Quinn Hughes or Jonas Brodin, and Olli Maatta and Zach Bogosian together on the third pair. A win against the Bruins would add to a 10-game point streak and mark seven straight road victories all without Brock Faber. What are MN Wild getting back with Faber’s return? Last season, the Maple Grove native had career highs of 15 goals and 51 points in 80 games, with 36 assists and a plus-18. His 15 goals led Wild defensemen and tied for 10th among all NHL defensemen. Faber averaged 24:41 of ice time, second on the team behind Hughes. He’s now in year two of an eight-year, $68 million contract that carries an $8.5 million cap hit through 2032-33. Faber and the Wild face the Bruins (13-5-1) tonight at 6 p.m. CT at TD Garden on Wild+ and Fubo. Russo reported that Jesper Wallstedt will start in goal against Jeremy Swayman. item.title: Minnesota Vikings’ Kirk Cousins Trade Features Interesting Twist
item.description: The Minnesota Vikings made a move to acquire quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders at the NFL trade deadline, sending a third-round pick to the Raiders in return. The deal followed the Vikings’ miserable Week 9 Monday night loss to the Buffalo Bills, where Minnesota managed just six points in a 17-point defeat. Carson Wentz managed just 81 passing yards before being benched for Max Brosmer. That appeared to be the tipping point for the Vikings, who started the 2026 campaign 6-0 but have now lost two games in a row to watch their NFC North lead disappear. However, Minnesota had apparently reached a boiling before before the Bills loss, according to NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport. Minnesota Vikings tried to trade for Kirk Cousins earlier Oct 23, 2023; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) warms up before the game against the San Francisco 49ers at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeffrey Becker-USA TODAY Sports Evidently, the Vikings reached out to the Raiders before Monday night’s disaster. “The first time the Vikings reached out to the Raiders about a potential trade for Kirk Cousins was midday Monday, hours before Minnesota played the Bills on ‘Monday Night Football,’ league sources told ESPN and NFL Network,” Schefter and Rapoport wrote . “During that call, the Vikings made it clear to the Raiders that they wanted to see how Monday night went first before having any further conversations about Cousins, but they would be in touch if needed.” Obviously, things ended up going very south for the Vikings in that game, so that was when they ultimately decided to pull the trigger. Of course, Minnesota may have incidentally given Las Vegas more leverage in those trade discussions considering just how bad the Vikings looked under center on Monday, but a third-round pick seemed like a small price to pay for Minnesota. Cousins is now in his second stint with the Vikings after spending six years with the club between 2018 and 2023. The 38-year-old is certainly armed with an impressive stable of weapons in Minnesota, so we’ll see if he can ultimately lead the Vikings on a deep playoff run. item.title: 'He actually got emotional': R Ashwin reveals Virat Kohli's reaction to his retirement decision
item.description: Ravichandran Ashwin has opened up about an emotional conversation with Virat Kohli at the Gabba during the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy, recalling how the former India captain was left emotional after learning about his decision to retire from international cricket. The former India off-spinner revealed that the conversation took place on the balcony in Brisbane during a rain interruption. What began as an informal discussion between the two eventually turned into a heartfelt exchange, with Kohli speaking about the future of India's Test team and the challenges surrounding its transition. Speaking on a podcast with Aakash Chopra, Ashwin explained that retirement had been on his mind for several months before he finally called time on his career in December 2024. He disclosed that he had first contemplated the decision as early as March 2024, despite enjoying an excellent run with the ball. However, persistent knee problems were affecting his batting. Head coach Gautam Gambhir subsequently urged him to continue until the end of India's 2024 home season. The home Test series against New Zealand, in which India suffered a whitewash, proved particularly disappointing for Ashwin. He felt he was no longer able to deliver match-winning performances for the team. His decision became firmer after he was left out of India's playing XI for the opening Test against Australia in Perth. When an opportunity arose during the Brisbane Test, Ashwin found himself alone with Kohli during a rain break and decided to share his thoughts. “In that game, I didn’t go there to tell Virat and it was raining; I sat with him only because he was sitting alone," Ashwin remembered. Ashwin also reflected on how his relationship with Kohli had evolved over the years. The two had experienced differences in the past, but the former spinner said their equation improved following the COVID break. During their conversation at the Gabba, Kohli began discussing his own batting, the state of the Indian Test side and the challenges ahead during a period of transition. “My relationship with Virat improved after the COVID break. I realized that if there were any disappointments in my mind, it wasn’t his fault. I tried to speak to him about that; I was forthcoming. I had nothing selfish to to say. But he started speaking his mind: what he was thinking about his batting, how he looked at the Indian Test team, what it needed in a transition. He was talking like a leader, how there were these basic problems in the team and so on. I listened." The conversation took an unexpected turn when Kohli sought Ashwin's opinion on the team's future. item.title: Give J.J. McCarthy a quicker late-game answer for the Giants
item.description: New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) looks to throw the ball during a game against the Washington Commanders at MetLife Stadium, Nov 12, 2026, East Rutherford, NJ, USA. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect On Friday, John Harbaugh said the Giants had short and deep routes available on the late throws against Washington’s all-out pressure. I’d change the order of the decision for J.J. McCarthy. With a field goal still useful and the clock running out, decide before the snap which underneath throw can keep the drive alive. Take the deep ball when the look is right, not because pressure narrowed the quarterback’s time to think. The pressure itself didn’t defeat McCarthy all night. He went 8-for-14 for 155 yards against the blitz, according to Next Gen Stats via John Schmeelk’s Friday review . He also finished with a career-high 293 passing yards. In the final sequence a deep throw intended for Malik Nabers was intercepted with 25 seconds left, per the game recap . You can see a quarterback handle extra rushers well for most of a game and still want a better answer for that last situation. Separate the pressure answer from the clock answer “The ball’s got to come out fast,” Harbaugh said . He noted the offense couldn’t block everyone on the zero blitzes and said McCarthy made split-second choices. A receiver can be open further down the field without being the best throw for the situation. To me, the adjustment is to give McCarthy a short route he can choose at the line and a clear idea of which side he needs the catch to finish on. Nov 12, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) shouts out a call during the second half against the Washington Commanders at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On a down when New York still has time to run another play, I’d bring a receiver across the formation and attach a break toward the boundary at the sticks. Use the movement to see a defender travel and make the throw early enough that the receiver can catch it facing the sideline. If the defense takes away the short route and leaves Nabers on top of his man with room to land the ball, the vertical throw stays in the call. The quarterback isn’t being asked to pass up a touchdown. He’s being asked to know what a useful completion looks like before the rush arrives. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. The Giants don’t need to take the deep ball away The alternative is to leave an extra blocker in and treat the play as a chance to hit a deeper route. I’d use that if New York needs a bigger gain, or if there isn’t a credible short route that will stop the clock. The price is one fewer receiver in the pattern, and even adding a blocker might not account for every rusher. Once the game comes down to a final pass, the trade-off changes again. item.title: Alec Bohm makes sense for the Yankees at one guaranteed year
item.description: Oct 1, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Philadelphia Phillies infielder Alec Bohm (28) looks on before game three of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Field. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alec Bohm is worth a call if the Yankees want a right-handed answer at third base. I wouldn’t sign him as the answer for all 162 games. My offer would be one guaranteed year, with Ryan McMahon still around to take most of the starts against right-handers and defend late when New York has a lead. MLB.com’s Mark Feinsand reported the Yankees’ interest , after Jon Heyman first reported it for the New York Post. Bryan Hoch’s Friday look at the roster says New York is open to adding at third. Neither report establishes a one-year offer. That’s the term I’d be willing to guarantee. Sep 30, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Philadelphia Phillies first baseman Alec Bohm (28) celebrates in the dugout after hitting a solo home run against the Atlanta Braves in the tenth inning during game two of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Yankees would be buying the matchup, not the entire stat line Bohm finished last season with a .698 OPS. Look at his 2026 splits and you can see two different jobs inside that number: .816 against left-handers in 192 plate appearances and .644 against right-handers in 437. McMahon had a .509 OPS against lefties and .662 against righties. The gap that gives Bohm a job is on the left-handed side of the opposing rotation. There isn’t much evidence in these numbers to make him the default against righties. The fielding is a separate reason not to hand him the full job. Feinsand’s report cites a minus-nine Fielding Run Value in 2026. That’s one measure and a down year, not an exact bill for what will happen in the Bronx. But if New York adds Bohm for the bat, it should be comfortable replacing him for defense when that advantage has already been used and the game is on the line. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. A flexible third-base plan still has a price There will be days the likely second pitcher matters as much as the starter. If the opponent starts a lefty but can go to a right-hander in the fourth, I would keep the option to hit for Bohm later. If McMahon is on the bench and the tying run is on second, you’ve still got a left-handed bat and the ability to finish the game with him at third. Before making the offer, I’d also map out the rest of the bench. Two third basemen are easier to carry if somebody else can cover second and short without starting a chain of substitutions. Bohm’s experience at first helps, but with Ben Rice already there, those innings don’t carry the same value to the Yankees as they might to another club. You can make a case for paying more if you think Bohm’s .794 OPS after the All-Star break is the hitter you’ll get for a whole season.

item.title: Rams Could Acquire 8-Year Veteran WR in Post-Deadline Move
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams are certainly facing an injury crisis at the wide receiver position. Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington are all on injured reserve, and while the Rams are 5-4 and still very much alive in the NFC playoff picture, their offense is on life support. Los Angeles did not add any wide receiver help at the NFL trade deadline, much to the chagrin of the fanbase. And in terms of free agency, the options are very thin at this time of year. However, Bleacher Report’s Moe Moton has identified a potential fit for Matthew Stafford and the Rams’ aerial attack: eight-year veteran receiver Darius Slayton. Los Angeles Rams could sign Darius Slayton New York Giants wide receiver Darius Slayton (18) runs with the ball, Sunday, January 4, 2026, in East Rutherford. Slayton was released by the New York Giants before the season. He then signed with the Indianapolis Colts, but was cut before even getting into a game. That leaves the door open for the Rams to sign him. “At 29, Slayton can be a productive perimeter playmaker if he can still stretch defenses in the vertical passing game,” Moton wrote . “… The Los Angeles Rams will be without their top two receivers, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, for the foreseeable future. Matthew Stafford needs an experienced starting wideout to target within the Rams’ depleted pass-catching unit.” Slayton spent the first seven years of his career with the Giants and was a reliable weapon for them, posting over 500 receiving yards in six of his seven campaigns. He also finished with over 700 yards four times. Last year, the former fifth-round pick caught 37 passes for 538 yards and a touchdown, although he struggled with drops. He also underwent core muscle surgery after the season. Slayton wouldn’t be anyone’s favorite option, but he could certainly be of help to a Rams team in dire need of help at the position. item.title: Columbus Blue Jackets coach Rick Bowness remains out with health issue
item.description: Rick Bowness will miss a second straight game due to an undisclosed health issue when the Blue Jackets play the Philadelphia Flyers on Nov. 14 at Nationwide Arena, and his return to the bench is uncertain as he undergoes medical evaluation. More: The Columbus Blue Jackets are still sputtering: Where's the beef? Blue Jackets president/general manager Don Waddell said Bowness, 71, is considered "day-to-day" until more is known about the situation. Bowness hasn't been ruled out for an upcoming four-game road trip that starts Nov. 17 against the New York Islanders, but he won't travel with the team Oct. 16 when it heads to New York. "He's doing more testing on Monday," Waddell said. "He was actually here [at the arena] this morning for a little bit. That's a good sign. He met with the coaches and [all] that. We'll list him like a player, 'day-to-day,' but I've talked to him a lot. He's doing OK. He's just got some things that are affecting him that we need to figure out ... the doctors need to figure out." Bowness missed the Blue Jackets' 3-1 loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning on Oct. 12 at Nationwide Arena. Assistant coach Don Granato, former head coach of the Buffalo Sabres, handled the head coaching duties. Granato will again run the bench against the Flyers, while assistants Trent Vogelhuber, Jared Boll and goaltending coach Niklas Backstrom will handle their usual tasks. Waddell said the issue became noticeable recently, which led to Bowness getting checked out. "The last couple days, he wasn't feeling great," Waddell said. "He came in Thursday morning, and we told him to go home and get rest because he wasn't 'looking great, and from there we got our doctors involved and we're trying to figure out what's going on." Bowness left retirement to join the Blue Jackets in January 2026, taking over midseason for Dean Evason. His prior coaching job was with the Winnipeg Jets and he cited undisclosed family and health issues as the reason he stepped down from that head coaching role in April 2024. He twice stepped away from the Jets in 2023-24 for family and medical reasons. The first was after his wife, Judy, had a seizure and the second was for a minor medical procedure of his own. Upon joining the Blue Jackets, Bowness said he was physically up to returning as an NHL head coach and that his wife was just as eager for him to do it. item.description: Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock and his wife, Natalie Lock, announce exciting personal news before the Raiders game. Getty The Seattle Seahawks were expected to defend their Super Bowl title in a stacked NFC West division this year, but instead they have stumbled through the first half of the season and could join another expected powerhouse in missing the playoffs. John Breech of CBS Sports offered some “bold” predictions on the back half of the NFL season, suggesting that both the Seahawks and rival Los Angeles Rams will miss the postseason. His warning to Seattle centers on the team’s shaky quarterback play, with veteran backup Drew Lock forced into action. Seattle Risks Missing Playoffs in Super Bowl Defense Season Breech noted that Seattle’s struggles start with the quarterback, both Sam Darnold and Lock. “As for the Seahawks, quarterback play has hampered their season, and it doesn’t look like things are going to get much better on that front,” Breech wrote. “Sam Darnold has struggled all year, and to make matters worse, he’s been banged up. Drew Lock has been serviceable during his time on the field, but he doesn’t exactly make you feel good about this offense. It’s hard to see the QB spot improving, and if it doesn’t, the Seahawks could end up missing the playoffs.” The schedule makes the challenge even greater, Breech added. The Seahawks still have two games against the Rams, who are shaking off a slow start and have won three straight games. That puts pressure on both the Seahawks and Rams, Breech wrote. “If one team sweeps that series, that will pretty much eliminate the other team,” Breech noted. “If they split the series, both teams would have to go at least 5-2 in their seven other games just to get to 10-7. In the NFC this year, there’s no guarantee that 10-7 is going to get in the playoffs.” Drew Lock Playing Through Injuries As Tim Booth of the Seattle Times noted, Lock is playing through both an elbow injury and an oblique strain, though has been cleared to play for Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders. “The oblique thing doesn’t seem to be much of a concern and the elbow has been improving over the course of the last few weeks,” said Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury. “So, he’s actually taking more reps this week than he was going into last week. Five years of dominance, taking care of business against its smaller crosstown rival. A “little brother” of sorts. That was not the case on Friday night. In fact, the roles were reversed. Northwestern was the “little brother.” Literally. Both smaller in size and in depth, the Blue Demons exposed the Wildcats’ Achilles’ heel in their 20-point win. “Our offense really struggled tonight,” said head coach Chris Collins in his postgame presser. “A lot of it had to do with [DePaul]: their switching, their physicality, their ball pressure. I thought when the game was in the balance, we had a number of opportunities where we left points on the table in the open floor.” Separation was nowhere to be found for NU in this one; its largest lead was two points, and it’s because of personnel. DePaul’s pair of 7-footers Fabian Flores and Magoon Gwath anchored the Blue Demon defense, combining for 14 rebounds and four blocks on the night. DePaul finished with 45 and 11 in those categories, respectively, as its guards supplemented its play down low with relentless aggression and physicality, turning the game into a complete scrap. And Depaul won in the margins where Northwestern lacked. Collins didn’t avoid that. He took responsibility for it. “[Ade] Popoola had three offensive rebounds, [Noah] Meeusen had four — he’s the point guard. [He] wasn’t 7-foot. That’s seven offensive rebounds from their two guards. It was perhaps also the greatest rugby shock since Japan stunned South Africa at the 2015 World Cup, given the contrasting state of both countries heading into the clash. item.description: Nations Championship Wales (21) 35 Tries: T Williams, Lake, Griffin, James, Rees-Zammit Cons: Costelow 5 New Zealand (21) 28 Tries: Ratima, Sititi, Fineanganofo, Lakai Cons: Mo'unga 4. Wales celebrated a first victory against New Zealand in 73 years with a brilliant performance to spark astonishing scenes in Cardiff. Steve Tandy's unfancied side lifted a nation as they broke a 34-match losing sequence against the All Blacks that stretched back to 1953. In a nine-try Nations Championship thriller at the Principality Stadium, Wales led 14-0, 21-7 and 35-21 before they held off New Zealand with a wonderful defensive display in the final quarter, led by flankers James Botham and Jac Morgan and lock Dafydd Jenkins. The home side produced a stunning start with tries from inspirational scrum-half Tomos Williams and captain Dewi Lake inside the first six minutes. Prop Archie Griffin also added a first-half try, but New Zealand responded with scores from scrum-half Cortez Ratima, number eight Wallace Sititi and wing Fehi Fineanganofo to level the score 21-21 at half-time. Wales centre Eddie James and wing Louis Rees-Zammit scored early second-half tries before New Zealand flanker Peter Lakai pulled one back. The remarkable Wales defence followed as they held up the All Blacks three times over the line to stop New Zealand scoring, to evoke wild celebrations. Good things come to those who wait Wales had won the first three games in this fixture in 1905, 1935 and 1953 but have had to wait more than seven decades for the next. In 1953 the New Zealand dollar did not exist, Cardiff was not the capital city of Wales and tries were only worth three points. Sections of the New Zealand media had belittled Welsh rugby before the game, while some bookmakers offered odds of 20-1 for a Wales victory. Legends such as Sir Gareth Edwards, Alun Wyn Jones, Shane Williams, JPR Williams, Barry John and Phil Bennett had never enjoyed success against New Zealand in a Welsh jersey. Now Tandy's class of 2026 have written their own chapter in Welsh rugby's history. The 55,152 was the lowest crowd in the 14 matches between Wales and New Zealand at the Principality Stadium. item.title: Former Crosby coach Jason Martinez hired to lead athletics at Waterbury's 4 public high schools
item.description: Former Crosby High football player and coach Jason Martinez has been named director of athletics for the city of Waterbury, overseeing the four public high schools. (Courtesy of the Martinez family) WATERBURY - As a senior captain of the 1994 Crosby High football team, Jason Martinez was revered as a leader and a protector of what made being part of a team special. "There were always influences around us, but Jay was always that guy that made sure his teammates were making the right decisions at the right time," said Tony Ortiz, the iconic star running back and linebacker of that team. "He protected me on the offensive line, but he definitely had that mentality off the field, as well." More than three decades later, Martinez has the opportunity to bring that same leadership to student-athletes across one of the state's largest school districts. Thursday night, the Waterbury Board of Education and superintendent of schools Dr. Darren Schwartz announced that they had hired Martinez for the newly created director of athletics position. Martinez will oversee the four current athletic directors in the city: David Ieronimo (Crosby), Joseph Del Debbio (Kennedy), Ryan McDonald (Waterbury Career Academy) and Alan Piccolo (Wilby). A longtime football coach, Martinez spent the last five years as an assistant principal at Wilby High. He missed athletics and saw the citywide athletic director's job as a chance to combine his passion for sports with his educational leadership. "Being out of athletics for a few years, a piece of me was missing," Martinez said. "I am most comfortable on an athletic field or in a gym. I felt like I was put on this planet to be in those spaces and help people understand how important they are. So, this chance to get back to my roots with the power to connect an entire district is a lifelong dream." Schwartz shares Martinez's belief in the value of sports. "Sports were instrumental in my own development, leadership and social-emotional growth," Schwartz said. "... For me, athletics can be a draw that helps many students keep coming to school every day. It also gives them intangible skills that are important when they leave our system and enter the workforce or pursue higher education." Schwartz said Waterbury wasn't maximizing the potential of its four public high schools because they operated separately and were disconnected from the city's middle schools and youth sports organizations. He believes uniting the programs through common goals, leadership and accountability could increase their impact on student-athletes. He sees five ways a districtwide athletic director could help the schools expand opportunities: Create a consistent sportsmanship and behavior program. Work with the city's Parks and Recreation Department, the YMCA, Boys & Girls Club and PAL to provide athletic opportunities in middle school and build programs that feed into high schools. Use the district's purchasing power to buy uniforms and equipment collectively.

item.title: How FAA's ground stop impacts Saturday's college football schedule
item.description: While Texas will play as scheduled on Saturday at LSU, Oklahoma's game against Ole Miss was pushed back to Sunday after Friday's ground stop that halted air travel and impacted college football teams' travel plans. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) The ground stop that halted air travel for a few hours Friday shook up Saturday's college football schedule, even resulting in a rare Sunday game. Locally, the most notable change is Rice pushing its kickoff against Tulane back from 1 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. as the Green Wave had to travel by bus from New Orleans for the game at First Community Stadium. While No. 6 Texas had a delayed departure for its game at No. 21 LSU, that will still begin at 6:30 p.m. in Baton Rouge, La. Texas A&M is at home against No. 8 Tennessee and will still kick off at 2 p.m. after the Volunteers traveled to College Station late Friday. ALSO SEE: Saturday's college football TV schedule Baylor's game at No. 10 BYU was pushed back to a 6 p.m. start in Provo, Utah. It was originally scheduled for 2:30 p.m. The game could not be rescheduled to Sunday because BYU is not allowed to play on Sundays due to religious observances by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, which runs the school. The University of Houston was not impacted as the Cougars played Friday night and lost at Colorado. The most notable change is the Ole Miss-Oklahoma game being moved to noon Sunday, marking the rare college football game played on Sunday during the NFL season. Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny said in a statement that Ole Miss "explored every avenue to travel to Norman and play on Saturday as planned," but "they were unable to find a solution." Denny said the Sooners made a "strong objection" to playing on Sunday but were told a failure to play would result in a forfeit. "Rescheduling the game has a significant impact, particularly on our fans," Denny said. "Those who have made travel arrangements, accommodations and personal plans around a Saturday game now face unnecessary disruption and hardship. Their time, commitment and investment deserve greater consideration than they were afforded in the conference's decision tonight. "I understand that difficult decisions sometimes must be made under extraordinary circumstances. But those decisions must also consider the impact on everyone involved. Put simply, this decision isn't fair to our athletes, our institution or to Sooner Nation. But we've been given no other choice. We are obligated to play the game when directed, but we remain steadfast in our belief that the wrong outcome was reached this evening. We will continue to fight in the best interests of OU Athletics and always on behalf of our student-athletes and fans." Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle.
